result.summary: Fixes Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) warnings across fuzz tests and test utilities in `src/test/fuzz`, and configures CI to treat any future IWYU warnings in these directories as errors. It separates the `NodeId` declaration into a dedicated `node/node_id.h` header to resolve symbol ambiguity for tooling, updates related headers in `net` and `node/eviction`, and adds a lint check enforcing that all code in headers is inside include guards.
result.problem: Fuzz tests rely on transitive header inclusions, leaving include lists incomplete and causing IWYU static analysis in CI to fail or remain unenforced for `src/test/fuzz`. Furthermore, duplicate declarations of types like `NodeId` make header ownership ambiguous for static analysis tools.
evidence: PR description: 'This PR continues the ongoing effort to enforce IWYU warnings. See Developer Notes.'
Commit 86296b1bf6: 'Two identical declarations of NodeId make it ambiguous for static tools such as IWYU which header should provide the symbol.'
result.scope_notes: Very large diff across 194 files, but the vast majority of changes are mechanical additions, removals, and reorderings of `#include` directives and forward declarations in fuzz test targets.
result.changed_since_previous: Now includes full patch and diff inspection; the commits and technical approach remain identical to the previous version.
result.card: Fixes Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) warnings across fuzz tests in src/test/fuzz and enables error enforcement for them in CI. It also introduces node/node_id.h to resolve duplicate declaration ambiguity for tooling and adds a linter requiring header code to remain within include guards. This continues an ongoing internal code-hygiene and maintenance initiative to eliminate transitive header dependencies. The PR is marked as a draft and is explicitly based on PRs #36805 and #36807.

risk.why: Mistakes could cause build failures or header re-inclusion errors on certain compilers, but cannot affect runtime behavior or consensus.
